'''Ruth Durrer''' (born 1958) is a professor of [[Cosmology]] at the [[University of Geneva]]. She works on the [[cosmic microwave background]], [[brane cosmology]] and [[massive gravity]].

== Early life and education ==
Durrer was born in [[Kerns, Switzerland|Kerns]].<ref name=":2" /> She earned her high school diploma at Kantonales Lehrerseminar, and studied at the [[University of Zurich|University of Zürich]].<ref name=":2" /> She completed her PhD on [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbation theory]] with [[Norbert Straumann]] at the [[University of Zurich|University of Zürich]] in 1988.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://cosmology.unige.ch/users/ruth-durrer|title=Ruth Durrer {{!}} Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics - University of Geneva|website=cosmology.unige.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=105798|title=Ruth Durrer - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.ams.org|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Cambridge]] for a year, before joining [[Princeton University]] in 1989.<ref name="Ruth Durrer">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/ruth-durrer|title=Ruth Durrer|website=Institute for Advanced Study|language=en|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> Durrer returned to [[Zürich]] in 1991, completing a postdoctoral fellowship.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Durrer was made an assistant professor at the [[University of Zürich]] in 1992, and full professor at the [[University of Geneva]] in 1995.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fiteoweb.unige.ch/~durrer/|title=Ruth's Homepage|website=fiteoweb.unige.ch|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> She is a member of the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://perimeterinstitute.ca/people/ruth-durrer|title=Ruth Durrer {{!}} Perimeter Institute|website=perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> She works on the [[cosmic microwave background]] and [[massive gravity]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=The cosmic microwave background|last=Durrer, Ruth.|date=2008|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-511-42406-9|location=Cambridge, UK|oclc=297170401}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nccr-swissmap.ch/people/ruth-durrer|title=Ruth Durrer {{!}} SwissMAP|website=www.nccr-swissmap.ch|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://courses.ipht.cnrs.fr/?q=fr/node/74|title=Cosmology and the cosmic microwave background {{!}} Cours de physique théorique|website=courses.ipht.cnrs.fr|access-date=2019-04-28|publisher=[[Institut de physique théorique - IPhT Saclay]]}}</ref> [[Massive gravity]] describes an expanding universe with massive [[graviton]]s, which weakens gravity on large scales.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.colloquium.phys.ethz.ch/programme/previous/autumn15/durrer.html|title=Ruth Durrer|website=www.colloquium.phys.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> Durrer uses [[cosmological]] observations as a test for [[general relativity]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://media.ed.ac.uk/media/Testing+General+Relativity+with+Cosmological+observations+-+Ruth+Durrer/1_f2yvcrn0|title=Testing General Relativity with Cosmological observations - Ruth Durrer|website=Media Hopper Create - The University of Edinburgh Media Platform|language=en|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref>

Durrer has contributed extensively to the theoretical understanding of [[topological defect]]s. She showed that cosmic textures can suppress the [[Cosmic microwave background#Primary anisotropy|acoustic peak]]s of the angular [[Power spectra|power spectrum]] of the [[cosmic microwave background]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Durrer|first1=Ruth|last2=Gangui|first2=Alejandro|last3=Sakellariadou|first3=Mairi|date=1996-01-22|title=Doppler Peaks in the Angular Power Spectrum of the Cosmic Microwave Background: A Fingerprint of Topological Defects|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=76|issue=4|pages=579–582|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.579|pmid=10061495|arxiv=astro-ph/9507035|bibcode=1996PhRvL..76..579D|s2cid=16031907}}</ref> This results confirm that cosmic textures are not responsible for the distribution of matter in the observed universe. She worked with [[Neil Turok]] to demonstrate it is possible to use terrestrial lab-based experiments to test [[cosmological phase transitions]] in the early universe.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Yurke|first1=Bernard|last2=Turok|first2=Neil|last3=Durrer|first3=Ruth|last4=Chuang|first4=Isaac|date=1991-03-15|title=Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals|journal=Science|language=en|volume=251|issue=4999|pages=1336–1342|doi=10.1126/science.251.4999.1336|issn=0036-8075|pmid=17816188|bibcode=1991Sci...251.1336C|s2cid=33894124}}</ref> These include using [[liquid crystal]]s to study the scaling solutions of string networks.<ref name=":3" /> She has also demonstrated that density fluctuations in the early universe can result in the [[cosmological]] [[magnetic field]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Durrer|first=Ruth|date=2006-02-10|title=Is the Mystery of Cosmic Magnetic Fields Solved?|journal=Science|language=en|volume=311|issue=5762|pages=787–788|doi=10.1126/science.1122395|issn=0036-8075|pmid=16469908|s2cid=1522770|url=http://archive-ouverte.unige.ch/unige:946}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg19125671-700-north-of-the-big-bang/|title=North of the Big Bang|website=www.newscientist.com|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201005/members.cfm|title=Members in the Media|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> She showed that the scaling properties of these primordial [[magnetic field]]s can be determined by [[Causality conditions|causality]] arguments alone.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Durrer|first1=Ruth|last2=Caprini|first2=Chiara|date=2003-11-19|title=Primordial magnetic fields and causality|journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics|volume=2003|issue=11|page=010|doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2003/11/010|issn=1475-7516|arxiv=astro-ph/0305059|bibcode=2003JCAP...11..010D|s2cid=53768021}}</ref>

Durrer studied an extended area of space, separating it into 60 billion zones and using the [[c++]] library LATfield2 with a [[supercomputer]] to study the movement of individual particles.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://dailygalaxy.com/2016/03/spacetime-and-gravitational-waves-yield-a-new-view-of-the-universe/|title=Spacetime and Gravitational Waves Yield a New View of the Universe|date=2016-03-07|website=The Daily Galaxy|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> She used [[Einstein's equation]]s to calculate the distance in [[metric space]], comparing this with the prediction of [[Newton's method]]s.<ref name=":1" /> She has investigated [[dark energy]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Durrer Ruth|date=2011-12-28|title=What do we really know about dark energy?|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences|volume=369|issue=1957|pages=5102–5114|doi=10.1098/rsta.2011.0285|pmid=22084297|bibcode=2011RSPTA.369.5102D|doi-access=free|arxiv=1103.5331}}</ref>

Durrer was elected to Academia Net by the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] in 2012.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-ruth-durrer/1163466|title=Prof. Ruth Durrer - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref> She is a member of the committee of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iupap.org/commissions/affiliated-commissions/ac-2-international-commission-on-general-relativity-and-gravitation/members/|title=AC2: Members {{!}} IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|website=iupap.org|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> She has held visiting academic positions at [[University of California, Berkeley]], [[Princeton University]], [[University of Paris-Sud]] and [[Galileo Galilei]] Institute.<ref name=":2" />

=== Awards and honours ===
Her awards and honours include;

* 1992 [[Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences|Swiss Academy of Sciences]] Schaefli Award<ref name="Ruth Durrer"/>
* 2024 [[Prix Jules Janssen]] awarded by the [[Société astronomique de France]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://saf-astronomie.fr/en-janssen-prize/|title=Prix Jules Janssen|website=Société astronomique de France|language=en}}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Durrer is married with three children.<ref name=":2" />
She speaks German, English, French, and Swiss German.<ref name=":2" />
